storm.summary_layperson: No storms nearby this evening — it stays dry through 10 PM, with showers arriving late tonight and a better chance of strong thunderstorms tomorrow (Friday) evening.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer at any point tonight: the Sound (65°F) is already about 2°F warmer than the air at 4 PM, and that reversed gap widens to about 7°F by 7 PM as the air cools.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: quiet for the evening window. KOKX radar shows no echoes at all in range, there are no NWS alerts, and the HRRR model has zero instability (CAPE 0 J/kg) over the cove through 10 PM. Upper-level winds are strong (0–6 km shear near 49 kt from the west), but with no instability there is nothing for that shear to organize.

Local modifier: none in play. The protective marine layer only works when the Sound is noticeably cooler than the air — at least about 5°F — so that a shallow, stable layer of cool air sits over the water and chokes incoming storms. Today it's the other way around: Sound water is 64.9°F and the air at Riverside YC is 62.7°F. After sunset (6:13 PM) the air keeps cooling while the Sound holds its temperature, so the gap runs further in the wrong direction (about −6°F at 6 PM and −7°F at 7 PM). The cove has no buffer tonight, but with no storms around, that doesn't matter this evening.

What's coming: the NWS forecast discussion from Upton has a warm front bringing showers and possibly a few thunderstorms late tonight into Friday morning, after this window. The bigger event is Friday evening: a squall line along a cold front, timed for roughly 5–7 PM at the western edge of the forecast area, with SPC's slight risk for severe storms (damaging wind gusts the main threat), mainly NE New Jersey and the Lower Hudson Valley. The line should push offshore around 9–11 PM Friday.

Most likely outcome for the cove tonight: dry through 10 PM, same as surrounding towns. Clouds and the first showers come in overnight.

What would change the call: showers or storms forming on radar to the west or southwest before 10 PM (the warm front arriving early), or any NWS watch being issued for tonight. Neither is indicated now. For Friday, watch for the Sound turning cooler than the air ahead of the squall line — that's the only setup in which the cove gets any relief relative to inland towns.

wind.regime_label: Light southeasterly gradient wind — no sea breeze

hourly.shift_note: backing to SE, softest around sunset

wind.tactics_blurb: Near-drifter while there's light — 3–4 kt from S to SE, backing toward SE through sunset, so postponement risk is real. If you race, head for the west side of the course (right going upwind), away from the light, shifty air in the Greenwich Point shadow.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Regime: light gradient wind, no sea breeze. A sea breeze needs the land to be clearly warmer than the water. Today the air–water temperature difference is −2.3°F (air 62.6°F inland, Sound 64.9°F), so there's no thermal engine at all. The breeze in the cove is weak background flow from the south-southeast, ahead of a warm front due overnight. Mean wind at the authoritative stations is only 5 kt, and Riverside YC reads 3.2 kt gusting 6.5 from SSW (196°).

Direction: unsettled now, settling later. The models have SSE (about 160°) while the western-Sound stations median SSW (about 199°), a 40° gap, and only about 20% of stations agree on direction. That's normal for wind this light; it's local eddying, not a real shift you can play. Because this is a gradient-wind day, the sea-breeze direction correction doesn't apply. The forecast follows the models: S to SSE early, backing to a steadier SE (135–140°) by 7 PM as the background flow ahead of the front takes over.

Where the pressure is: in S–SE flow the west side of the course has the better pressure, upwind of the Greenwich Point shadow. The east side toward Tod's Point is lighter and shiftier. Going upwind that's the right-hand side. Don't expect clean persistent shifts; the swing toward SE is gradual over hours, not a race-length trend.

Through sunset (6:13 PM): there's no sea breeze to collapse, so no sharp shutdown. Expect the wind to stay at 3–4 kt through the 6–7 PM hours, with the cooling air over the warmer Sound adding a little patchiness. After dark the southeasterly fills to 6–7 kt (gusts near 10) by 8–10 PM as the warm front approaches. That's more breeze, but too late for evening racing.

What racers will feel: 3–4 kt is drifter territory: dinghies can move, keelboats will struggle, and a race committee could reasonably postpone or shorten. No backdoor front: Boston is SE, Providence a light northerly at 3 kt, and Groton S at 8 kt, so nothing is driving a sudden NE surge. The real weather comes overnight (showers) and Friday evening (a possible squall line). Neither touches this window.

data_caveats: The latest HRRR model run (19Z) only covered up to 8 PM when we fetched it. The 9–10 PM forecast comes from the previous run (18Z, 7–8 hours out), so it's less certain.
The HRRR model doesn't give gust values. Gusts are estimated from the gust-to-average ratio at Riverside YC.
Wind direction is poorly agreed across stations (about 20% agreement), and HRRR (SSE 159°) differs from the western-Sound stations (SSW 199°) by 40°. Early-window directions are low confidence.
Buoy 44040 (Western LIS) is offline: the UConn data server could not be reached.
The Farmingdale (KFRG) wind sensor is down, so that station is excluded.
